comparison: Both strongly support the chloroplast budding observations from live-cell imaging (C2, C3, C26-C33). OpenEval additionally evaluates C34-C36 (stroma volume decrease), which peer reviewers address separately in R8. Both emphasize high-quality imaging and internal consistency of the data.

OpenEval R1 includes quantitative stroma volume data (C34-C36) as part of the broader budding evidence. Peer R8 specifically validates these volume measurements, noting they strengthen the manuscript through quantification.

Both support the compositional claims about RCBs containing envelope markers but lacking thylakoid markers (C37-C43). OpenEval includes C44 (consistency with EM studies) which peer reviewers do not explicitly address. Both emphasize the quality of multi-marker imaging.

Perfect agreement on RCB trafficking dynamics and vacuolar delivery (C45-C50). Both highlight the transient tonoplast engulfment observation and praise the time-lapse imaging quality. The claim sets match exactly.

Both support the negative result that chloroplast protrusions do not increase in atg mutants (C4, C5, C51-C53). Peer R2 additionally includes C62 (autophagosome association quantification). Both accept this as demonstrating autophagy-dependence of the budding process.

Both support the temporal correlation between isolation membrane development and chloroplast budding (C6-C8, C54-C59). Peer R3 additionally evaluates C60-C67 (quantification of autophagosome marker association), which OpenEval addresses separately in R6. Both emphasize this as a key contribution with solid quantification.

OpenEval R6 focuses on quantitative autophagosome marker association data (C60-C67). Peer R3 includes these claims as part of the broader ATG8 co-localization finding (C6-C8, C54-C67). Both support the conclusion that autophagy substantially contributes to chloroplast degradation.

Minor overlap on C62 (autophagosome association). OpenEval R6 provides detailed evaluation of the quantitative association data, while peer R2 briefly mentions autophagy-dependence as part of the broader acceptance of the atg mutant results.

Both support the SA contribution to stromule formation in atg mutants (C69-C74, C76). OpenEval additionally evaluates C68 (hypothesis) and C75 (age-dependent effect). Peer reviewers accept the distinction between stromule formation and budding without challenge.

OpenEval R8 evaluates H2O2 measurements explaining residual stromules (C77-C81). Peer R7 includes C77-C81 as part of the broader stromule analysis. Both support these findings, with peer reviewers accepting the quantitative data without question.

Perfect agreement on DRP5B being dispensable for autophagy-related chloroplast division (C9, C82-C95). Both highlight this as a key finding distinguishing autophagy-related division from developmental division. The claim sets match exactly and both emphasize multiple lines of supporting evidence.

Both rate as UNCERTAIN the mechanistic claims about alternative division machinery (C11, C97). OpenEval R10 includes additional speculative claims (C96). Peer R9 explicitly notes the study does not reveal putative mechanisms, acknowledging these remain unresolved despite the negative results with DRP5B.

Strong overlap on speculative/mechanistic claims (C107, C109, C111, C112, C118, C122, C125, C132, C143, C151). Both rate these as UNCERTAIN or acknowledge them as unresolved. OpenEval explicitly identifies these as Discussion speculation, while peer reviewers note the mechanisms remain unrevealed.

Both support the conclusion that autophagy is the main pathway for chloroplast degradation during early sugar starvation (C113, C116). OpenEval R14 includes additional synthesis claims (C114, C115, C117). Peer R10 accepts this despite incomplete labeling, noting concerns were resolved through revision.

Minor overlap on C96 (stromule-related speculation). OpenEval R10 groups this with other mechanistic uncertainties, while peer R7 accepts the negative result about stromules without specifically addressing the speculative aspect of C96.

OpenEval R11 evaluates background literature citations (C1, C10, C12-C25) as appropriately supporting the study's foundation. Peer reviewers do not provide separate evaluation of these contextual claims, focusing instead on novel findings.

OpenEval R12 evaluates Discussion citations and comparisons to related fields (C98-C150, excluding speculative claims) as appropriately contextualized. Peer reviewers do not separately evaluate these contextual/comparative claims from the literature.

OpenEval R15 supports the inference about autophagy receptors (C124) based on imaging data and mechanistic understanding. Peer reviewers do not separately evaluate this specific inference, though it relates to the broader mechanistic gaps they identify.
